description: Answer a question the Cheap First way: Dolphin answers, another cheap sample checks numbers and choices, SERV Reasoning grades anything else, and a premium model answers instead only if the check misses the pass mark. Returns the answer, whether it escalated, the check score, the cost and the estimated saving. Free calls use the public demo limits (600 characters, 10 an hour per IP, 300 a day). Send Authorization: Bearer cf_... or an x402 payment of $0.005 USDC on Base for the paid limits (2000 characters). To receive the x402 challenge, send the header X-Cheap-First-Paid: 1. mode: strict escalates more often (pass mark 85), balanced is the default (75), budget escalates less often (60).

mode.description: strict, balanced (default) or budget. Unknown values are treated as balanced.

question.description: The question. 600 characters on the free demo, 2000 when paid.

name: ask_cheap_first

outputSchema.description: One Cheap First answer, plus what the check decided and what it cost.

answer.description: The answer to give the user.

answeredBy.description: cheap is Dolphin. premium is the frontier model.

checkReason.description: Why the check passed or failed, in one line.

checkScore.description: The checker's score for the cheap answer, from 0 to 100.

checkSignal.description: agreement: extra cheap samples. arithmetic: an equation did not evaluate. grader: the language-model grade. blank: Dolphin returned nothing.

costUsd.description: What Cheap First spent on this call, in US dollars.

creditsLeft.description: Prepaid answers left on the key, when one was used.

escalated.description: True when the check failed and the premium model answered instead.

model.description: Label of the model that produced the answer.

paidUsd.description: What the caller paid, on the paid tier.

savedUsd.description: Estimated saving against sending the question to the premium model alone. Can be negative when an escalation cost more than that.

transaction.description: x402 settlement transaction, when there is one.

title: Ask Cheap First
